q: What does the loop give you?
o: Small pieces of text, one after another
why: Each text delta is a few words. The stop reason and token counts come in the last events.

q: What is the content type of the response?
why: Server-sent events use text/event-stream, and the body is sent in chunks as it is produced.

q: What is the last event of a stream that went well?
why: The done event lets the client tell a finished answer from a stream that was cut.

c:
def events():
    yield 'data: "one "

'
    yield 'data: "two "

'
    raise RuntimeError("the model call failed")   # no try/except
q: What status code does the client see?
o: 200: it was sent before the first piece
why: The status goes out before the first piece, so a later failure cannot change it.

c:
# same broken stream
curl -s -N localhost:8045/broken > /dev/null; echo $?
q: What does curl say when the stream ends in a failure?
why: The connection ended before the response was complete. A client cannot tell that from a normal end, unless you send an error or done event.

q: Why is each piece sent as a JSON string?
o: So spaces and new lines inside a piece are kept safe
why: The quotes protect leading and trailing spaces and any new line in the piece.
